title: Water Cycle Conditions clarity
method: Frozen actual runtime in an owned ephemeral localhost server and isolated Chromium. Native ranges, choices, resets, preset scope, rendered geometry, system colors, shared-model readout agreement, and paused parcel / learner-work preservation. No learner tabs, port 8770, runtime edits, or Git writes.

detail.text: 100% is the model’s reference sunlight; a saved comparison baseline can differ.
Sunlight supplies the energy that lets liquid water become water vapor.
Temperature changes molecular motion and helps determine whether water is liquid, ice, or vapor.
1× is the model’s reference wind; a saved comparison baseline can differ.
Wind transports vapor and replaces moist surface air; it is not the cycle's energy source.
Teaching index, not a measured evaporation rate.
Science note: sunlight supplies energy, temperature affects molecular motion and phase, and wind transports vapor. Change one control at a time to make a fair comparison.
Relative rainfall intensity; this is a teaching input, not mm per hour.
How wet the soil is before this rain; this is a teaching index.
How easily water can pass through soil pores.

What covers the ground; vegetation and built surfaces affect both pathways.
Separate 0–100 teaching indices; arrows show direction, not water amounts.
The signals are balanced: compare runoff and infiltration rather than treating either as certain.
Try a one-control test: change one input, compare both indices, and reset before trying another condition.
